description: The line plot illustrates the “Harmful with Refusal Ratio” across four different vision-language model configurations evaluated on two benchmarks — FigStep and MMSafetyBench — as a function of an increasing x-axis value that ranges from approximately 128 to 1024, likely representing input context length or token budget. The y-axis, labeled “Harmful with Refusal Ratio,” spans from 0.1 to 0.6 in linear scale, indicating the proportion of harmful responses that were still accompanied by a refusal. Four distinct lines are plotted: LLaVA-1.5-7B on FigStep (blue circles, solid line) starts at ~0.22 and rises to ~0.47; Qwen2-VL-7B on FigStep (orange squares, solid line) begins at ~0.17 and increases to ~0.58; LLaVA-1.5-7B on MMSafetyBench (green triangles, solid line) starts near 0.08 and climbs to ~0.50; and Qwen2-VL-7B on MMSafetyBench (red diamonds, solid line) begins at ~0.26 and rises steeply to ~0.62. All lines show a generally increasing trend, with Qwen2-VL-7B on MMSafetyBench exhibiting the steepest growth and highest final value, while LLaVA-1.5-7B on MMSafetyBench starts lowest but converges near the middle of the range. The plot suggests that as the x-axis variable increases, the models tend to produce more harmful outputs even when refusing, with performance varying significantly by model and benchmark.
